title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook standardizes how the Developer Experience team creates and maintains SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for top support issues. It provides templates, review workflows, CI checks, and a prioritized list of common production issues with step-by-step remediation.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce time-to-value for engineers adopting Redwood APIs and minimize repeat support overhead by shipping consistent, well-tested docs and examples.
- Scope: All SDK guides, language quickstarts, CLI examples, docs-site pages, and the canonical troubleshooting entries owned by eng-developer-experience. Does not cover product PRDs or internal-only runbooks owned by other teams.

Owner and reviewers:
- Primary owner: Developer Experience (eng-developer-experience)
- Doc steward: Aisha Patel (author)
- Reviewers: Laura Chen, Ravi Singh
- Publishing approver: Docs lead (engineer on-call for devex)

High-level artifacts produced by this playbook:
- SDK Guide (per-language): installation, authentication, usage patterns, error handling, examples, table of supported API versions.
- Quickstart (per-language): 5–10 minute end-to-end example with a reproducible repository link.
- API Example Snippets: copy-paste-ready REST and SDK snippets for common flows (chat, streaming, embeddings, reranking).
- Docs site procedure: templates, publishing checklist, CI linting, and release notes rules.
- Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes: curated pages for the highest-frequency problems with tested remediation steps.

Quickstart and SDK guide templates (required sections):
1) Title and one-line summary
2) Prerequisites (versioned CLI, SDK version, account, API key, region)
3) Quick start steps (numbered: install, auth, run example, validate output)
4) Code snippets (minimum: REST, Python, JavaScript; optional: Go, Java)
5) Configuration table (required env vars, timeouts, memory suggestions)
6) Troubleshooting and FAQ (link to canonical fixes)
7) Ownership and last-updated metadata

Example configuration table (copy into every quickstart):
| Key | Example value | Purpose | SLO impact if absent | Owner |
|-----|---------------|---------|----------------------|-------|
| REDWOOD_API_KEY | sk-XXXX | Authentication for API calls | High (requests fail) | devex |
| REDWOOD_REGION | us-west-2 | Route to low-latency region | Medium (increased latency) | infra |
| SDK_VERSION | 1.8.2 | Reference SDK version used in examples | Low | devex |

Minimum QA and CI checks for docs PRs:
- Linting: markdownlint or confluence-lint (config in repo)
- Build: static site build + smoke render test for the page
- Snippet verification: run Python and JS snippet runners against a lightweight sandbox account (use test API key with read-only quotas)
- Link check: verify internal and external links are valid
- Accessibility: basic contrast and header structure check
- Required metadata validation: title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated

Publishing workflow (docs-site operating procedures):
1. Create feature branch: devex/docs/<short-desc>
2. Author completes quickstart and runs local snippet verifier.
3. Open PR to docs-main with checklist filled.
4. Automated CI runs lint/build/snippet checks.
5. Assign two reviewers (including cross-team reviewer for API changes).
6. After approvals, merge and the docs CI will deploy to staging.
7. Smoke test on staging: run the quickstart against staging sandbox.
8. Schedule release to production during weekday morning window; tag release in changelog.

Quickstart lifecycle and cadence:
- Review cadence: every six months (automatic task assigned to doc owner)
- Triggered review: on SDK major version bump, API contract change, or when a top support issue references the page
- Deprecation: mark deprecated sections clearly; remove after 12 months with migration notes

How to add a new SDK quickstart (step-by-step):
1) Fork templates repo: repo/devex/quickstart-templates
2) Copy language template: templates/sdk-quickstart-<lang>.md -> content/<project>-<lang>.md
3) Fill metadata header and examples (include REST + 2 SDK examples)
4) Run snippet verifier: tools/snippet-runner --file content/<file>.md --key $DEVEX_TEST_KEY
5) Open PR and add reviewers: @devex-owner, @api-product-owner
6) Merge after CI succeeds and reviewers approve

Recommended example patterns and anti-patterns:
- Use short, focused examples that demonstrate one concept (auth, streaming, embeddings) rather than monolithic apps.
- Prefer explicit shapes/JSON examples for model inputs and expected outputs.
- Avoid including long dataset extracts in docs; link to synthetic samples.
- Always include expected error responses and HTTP status codes for REST examples.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (priority-ordered):
1) Issue: Authentication failures (401/403 in SDKs)
   Canonical fix:
   - Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and not expired.
   - Check key scope: ensure the key has the required product scopes (read/write/embeddings).
   - Command: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
   - If failure persists, rotate key and update CI secrets.

2) Issue: Excessive latency for small requests (chat completions)
   Canonical fix:
   - Confirm client is using appropriate region (REDWOOD_REGION).
   - Enable short-circuiting cache for common prefixes (see caching guide).
   - Use streaming responses when interactive latency is required (JS: await client.chat.stream(...)).

3) Issue: Tokenization/cost surprises (higher-than-expected token usage)
   Canonical fix:
   - Compare client tokenization against model tokenization (use tools/tokenize --model gptx-4).
   - Trim long system prompts and avoid sending full documents as system role.

4) Issue: SDK snippet fails due to breaking change in SDK minor version
   Canonical fix:
   - Pin SDK_VERSION in quickstart (example: pip install redwood-sdk==1.8.2).
   - Add a migration note in the top of the guide for the new method signatures.

5) Issue: Streaming disconnects or truncated responses
   Canonical fix:
   - Verify HTTP/2 or chunked-encoding support in client environment.
   - Check load balancer idle timeouts (set > 120s for long streams).

6) Issue: Embeddings mismatch (vectors different length or inconsistent similarity scores)
   Canonical fix:
   - Confirm model version: embedding model id must match in all code paths.
   - Recompute embeddings with the canonical preprocessor outlined in the quickstart.

7) Issue: Rate-limiting (429) during load tests
   Canonical fix:
   - Implement exponential backoff and jitter per the SDK helper (client.backoff.with_jitter()).
   - If sustained, request dedicated capacity via Redwood Dedicated (internal runbook link).

8) Issue: Docs snippet uses sensitive data or hard-coded keys
   Canonical fix:
   - Replace keys with placeholders and add an admonition about secrets.
   - Use the snippet verifier to ensure no secrets are present before merge.

Canonical fixes are stored as individual pages under quickstarts-and-templates/canonical-fixes/; when you update a fix, add a changelog entry and notify the support rotation channel (#devex-support).

Snippet verification examples (commands):
- Run Python snippet: python tools/snippet-runner.py --file examples/quickstart-python.md --backend sandbox --key $DEVEX_TEST_KEY
- Run JS snippet: node tools/snippet-runner.js --file examples/quickstart-js.md --key $DEVEX_TEST_KEY
- Verify REST example with curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'

Metrics and success criteria for the playbook:
- Decrease mean time-to-first-success (MTTFS) for new SDK users by 25% year-over-year.
- Reduce repeat support tickets referencing docs by 40% in 6 months after adoption of canonical fixes.
- Snippet verification coverage >= 85% of examples across languages.

Escalation and on-call guidance:
- If a doc-related incident impacts customers, tag #sre and #devex-support and follow the incident runbook.
- For repeated or high-severity support issues traceable to docs, schedule a postmortem and add an ADR to change the docs process.

Appendix: Common PR checklist (to paste in PR description):
- [ ] Metadata present (title, author, owner_team, created_at, last_updated)
- [ ] Snippets verified (Python, JS, REST)
- [ ] CI lint/build passed
- [ ] Two reviewers assigned and at least one cross-team reviewer
- [ ] Changelog entry added (if user-facing change)

Related resources and links:
- Quickstart templates repo: git@github.com:redwood/devex-quickstart-templates.git
- Docs site build: docs.redwood.ai (internal CI)
- Snippet runner tools: repo/tools/snippet-runner
- Support channel: #devex-support (Slack)

Contact: For questions about this playbook or ownership changes, contact the doc steward (Aisha Patel) or the Developer Experience engineering manager.

Last updated notes:
- 2026-07-12: Added streaming disconnect guidance and expanded CI snippet verification rules.
